overview: The council reviewed communication strategies for public outreach and received updates on several city initiatives, including the Electrify Medford program, curbside composting, and municipal infrastructure grants.

items.title: Minutes of Previous Meeting
items.summary: Approved the revised minutes of the previous meeting, which included corrections to the current meeting date and a plan to hold the June 24 session in person.

items.title: Meeting Schedule and Availability
items.summary: Decided to maintain the current Monday meeting schedule for the council after discussing potential alternatives to accommodate member availability.

items.title: City Communications and Outreach Strategy
items.summary: Emma from the city communications team provided an overview of municipal platforms available for program promotion, including robocalls, monthly newsletters, and partnerships with local media like the Medford Patch.

items.title: Stormwater Infrastructure Grants
items.summary: Approved repurposing a letter of support for a BRIC grant application and a revised MVP grant proposal focused on stormwater improvements at Tufts Park.

items.title: Electrify Medford and Electricity Aggregation
items.summary: Staff reported that energy coach training is beginning for the Electrify Medford program and announced a renewed electricity supply contract that increases renewable content while lowering costs for three years.

items.title: Curbside Composting Program
items.summary: Reported that over 1,800 residents have signed up for the no-cost composting program and announced a bulk compost and bin distribution event at City Hall on May 18.

items.title: Municipal Infrastructure and Energy Efficiency
items.summary: Updates were provided on a federal earmark request for a new resilience hub at the Willis-Appe Community Center and plans for HVAC electrification at the Andrews and McGlynn schools.

items.title: Community Events and Program Promotion
items.summary: Discussed upcoming energy code training for building inspectors, the use of a new electric street sweeper, and opportunities for tabling at the Haitian Flag Day celebration on May 18.
